engine.title: The multibagger screen qualified nobody for four weeks
engine.body: Corrects what this entry said on 2026-08-27. It read ‘the scan is running on schedule’ and blamed the fixed list on cadence. The ledger says otherwise: the last multibagger row is 2026-08-01, while magic, magicmagic and ai_longterm — the same Saturday job, the same slot — all logged 2026-08-22. Twenty-six days, three Saturdays, nothing written.
engine.note: The screen is not broken. Run on 2026-08-27 it took 11 candidates and rejected 10 for R:R below 2.0 — CHENNPETRO 1.29, FLUOROCHEM 1.07, GLAXO 0.59, which needs a 63% win rate merely to break even. The defect was that a week qualifying nobody wrote nothing at all, so the page served the 1 August list as though it were current. The attempt is recorded either way now. The gate is NOT loosened: publishing a 0.59 R:R to keep the section busy is the exact trade this screen exists to refuse, and an empty week is a real result.

engine.title: Stop buying strength that has already run
engine.body: The 4H RSI ceiling for longs was 75. Splitting every closed trade by the RSI recorded at entry showed the engine bleeding above 65 and profitable below it. The ceiling is now 65.
engine.note: Holds in both halves of the sample and at every cut point tested (60, 65, 70), so it is not one lucky threshold. The threshold was still chosen from this sample, so treat the size as an upper bound.

engine.title: A break-even stop would not have helped
engine.body: The median losing trade was +1.44R in profit before it reversed, and 59% touched a full +1R first. That looks like an obvious fix: move the stop to entry once price pays 1R. Re-walking every trade bar by bar, with winners subject to the same rule, says otherwise.
engine.note: The first version of this test only altered losers, which guarantees a positive answer. Correcting it reversed the conclusion. Nothing tested cleared one standard error, so no stop rule was adopted.

engine.title: Trades were being closed at prices that never traded
engine.body: The grader had never resolved a single trade — an exception was being swallowed silently — leaving a fallback path that could book an exit at a bar from before the signal existed. Every closed trade was re-graded against bars that actually printed.
evidence: exits corrected to a real price
engine.note: This moved the headline number against me. It is published anyway, because the earlier number was not real. Pre-correction data is kept in the repo rather than deleted.

engine.title: A first target must pay back the risk
engine.body: T1 was whichever structural level sat nearest the entry, with no distance test. One signal shipped a T1 worth 0.19R against its own stop, printed beside an R:R of 2.41 quoted off T2. T1 must now return at least 1R.

chess.title: Opening Principle #1: Control the Centre
chess.body: Place pawns on e4/d4 (White) or e5/d5 (Black). Pieces control more squares from the centre. A pawn on e4 controls d5 and f5. A pawn on the edge controls only 1 square. Open with 1.e4 or 1.d4 and you immediately claim space. This is the foundation of all chess strategy.

wisdom.title: Being Present
wisdom.body: Your daughter doesn't need a perfect father. She needs a present one. Put the phone down for 20 minutes when you get home. Look her in the eyes. Play on the floor. These moments are the whole point. Work can wait. She is growing every day whether you show up or not.

book.author: Annie Duke
book.lesson: Humans are wired for confirmation bias — we notice and remember information that confirms our existing beliefs and ignore or discount information that challenges them. Duke's remedy: actively seek people and information that disagree with you. Before committing to a position, ask 'what would have to be true for me to be wrong?' Find the strongest version of the opposing argument (steelmanning, not strawmanning). The goal is not to change your mind on everything — it's to update your beliefs proportionally to the evidence. Strong opinions, weakly held.
book.key_quote: Your best thinking comes from actively testing your beliefs against the strongest opposing evidence.
book.action: Before your next important decision, write the strongest possible case for the opposite position. Does it change your thinking?
crux: Every decision is a bet on an uncertain future. Certainty is not available.
Outcome ≠ decision quality. Chess is nearly all skill; life is poker — skill plus luck.
'Resulting' is judging a decision by how it turned out. It is the core error.
Replace true/false with a confidence percentage. 'I'm 70% on this' is honest and updatable.
Saying 'I'm not sure' is a strength. Pretended certainty blocks learning.
Beliefs are formed first and vetted later, if ever. Assume yours are unaudited.
Motivated reasoning: contradicting evidence gets scrutinised, confirming evidence gets waved through.
Self-serving bias: wins are skill, losses are luck. This makes experience useless.
Build a truth-seeking group with an explicit charter: accuracy over comfort, dissent welcomed.
Argue the other side properly. Steelman it, don't strawman it.
Separate signal from noise in feedback. A small sample tells you almost nothing.
Use temporal distance — 10 minutes, 10 months, 10 years — before deciding under emotion.
Backcast from success and pre-mortem from failure. Both, not one.
Tilt is real. Recognise the emotional state and stop deciding while in it.
learnings: A good decision can lose. A bad decision can win. Track process, not scoreboard.
Confidence expressed as a percentage is falsifiable. Confidence expressed as certainty is not.
Without separating luck from skill, ten years of experience teaches nothing.
You need people who will tell you that you were wrong.
examples: Pete Carroll's Super Bowl XLIX pass call was widely branded the worst in history. The interception rate on that play was about 2% — the decision was defensible, the outcome was not.
Duke won $4m at poker by focusing on decision quality across thousands of hands rather than the result of any single one.
In 1979, near-universal belief that Nixon's tapes would exonerate him did not survive contact with the tapes. Consensus is not evidence.
adapt: Log every trade with the thesis and a confidence %, not just entry and exit. The ledger is the point.
45.8% win rate at +0.171R is a good system. Judge it on 459 trades, not on last week.
After a losing trade, ask what a repeat of that decision returns over 100 tries. Usually the answer is 'fine'.
The 50% real win rate on the signals feed is the honest number. Publish that, not the flattering one.

minimalism.title: The Uniform
minimalism.body: Pick a small set of clothes that always work and buy multiples. Ends the morning decision, ends the mismatched purchase, ends the wardrobe that is 80% unworn.

etiquette.title: Write The Follow-Up
etiquette.body: After any meeting that mattered: three lines confirming what was agreed and who does what. It prevents disputes and marks you as the reliable one. Almost nobody does it.

stillness.title: Solitude Is Not Loneliness
stillness.body: Solitude is time free of other minds' input. It is where thinking happens. A room full of people and a phone full of voices are the same interruption.

model.title: Confirmation Bias
model.body: You will scrutinise disagreeing evidence and wave through agreeing evidence. Knowing this does not stop it. The only defence is to seek the counter-case deliberately.
model.action: Find the strongest argument against your current position. Steelman it.

drill.title: Mental Math: 1% Anchoring
drill.body: Compute 1% of a number, then scale. 1% of 847,000 is 8,470. So 3% is 25,410 and 0.5% is 4,235. Fluency here makes you visibly faster in meetings than people with better degrees.

dubai.title: Referral beats portal, by a lot
dubai.body: Applications through a company portal convert at low single digits. An internal referral converts an order of magnitude better. The list of people who can refer you is smaller than you think and you already know most of them.
dubai.targets: ICAI Dubai Chapter has roughly 4,000 members. That is the network.
dubai.action: Message five CAs already in the UAE. Ask for a 15-minute call, not a job.

father.title: Put the phone in another room
father.do: One 20-minute block a day with the phone physically out of sight.
father.why: Infants track gaze from very early. Divided attention is visible to her, and the research on 'still face' shows how quickly infants disengage when a caregiver's face goes flat.

father.title: Give her the spoon
father.do: Let her hold a second spoon while you feed her with the first.
father.why: It converts feeding from something done to her into something she participates in. Control over the process reduces resistance later, when refusal becomes a real phase.

life_wisdom.translation: Non-violence in thought, word and act
life_wisdom.teaching: The most demanding version is not physical — it is refusing to injure with speech or intent, including toward yourself.
life_wisdom.apply: Notice the sentence you would not say to a colleague, then check whether you say it to yourself about your own work. The standard should be the same.

life_wisdom.teaching: The fourth of the sublime states. Not indifference — full engagement without being destabilised by the outcome.
life_wisdom.apply: Judge the decision by the process you followed, not by how it turned out. A good decision with a bad outcome is still a good decision; conflating them is how you learn the wrong lesson.

interview_tech.q: Like-for-like sales are +3% but total sales are −2%. What is happening?
interview_tech.a: The existing estate is growing while the total base shrank — you closed stores, or a material store left the LFL set. LFL strips out openings and closures, so the gap is the net space effect. Ask: was the closure deliberate portfolio pruning, in which case −2% total with +3% LFL and better margin is a good outcome; or did leases expire without replacement, which is a pipeline failure. Follow with sales density per sqm — that tells you whether the remaining estate is genuinely stronger.

interview_tech.q: You are consolidating Malaysia and Indonesia. Where do FX translation differences land?
interview_tech.a: Functional currency results are translated at the closing rate for assets and liabilities, average rate for P&L, and the difference goes to other comprehensive income as a foreign currency translation reserve — not through P&L. It only recycles to P&L on disposal of the foreign operation. The trap: intercompany balances that are effectively permanent investment belong in the net investment, so their FX also goes to OCI. Getting that wrong puts noise through earnings every quarter.

interview_soft.a: They are screening for whether you have thought about it or are just leaving somewhere. Be concrete: the Gulf retail market's scale and the concentration of regional HQs; UAE corporate tax making the finance function genuinely more technical than it was; and the specific fit between your multi-country consolidation experience and a group operating across GCC markets. Do not lead with tax-free income or lifestyle — every candidate says it and none of it is about the job.

interview_soft.q: How do you prioritise when everything is urgent?
interview_soft.a: Give a working rule, not a philosophy. Something like: anything with a statutory deadline is non-negotiable; then anything that changes a decision being made this week; then anything that compounds — process fixes that stop the same fire recurring; then everything else. The part interviewers actually want: what you stopped doing and who you told. Prioritisation without explicit de-prioritisation is just a longer list.

cfo_field.q: Learn the lease standard properly. In the Gulf it is not a footnote.
cfo_field.a: IFRS 16 put every store lease on the balance sheet as a right-of-use asset and a lease liability. Two consequences a CFO must be able to say out loud: EBITDA is now flattered, because rent that used to sit in operating costs is split into depreciation and interest; and leverage ratios move even though nothing about the business changed. If your covenant is set on a pre-IFRS-16 basis, know it before the bank asks.

cfo_field.q: Automation without a control map is how a finance function loses its audit trail.
cfo_field.a: Before automating a process, write down: who can initiate, who approves, what the system does without a human, and where the exception report goes. Automation does not remove controls; it moves them from people to configuration, and configuration drifts silently. The question 'what breaks if this runs wrong for a month before anyone notices' is the one that separates a finance automation from a finance incident.

lichess_games.analysis: Focus on early pawn structure: after 1.e4 e6 2.d4 d5, avoid 3.Nc3 (the Winawer) and instead play 3.Nd2, then 4.e5 to lock the center, preventing Black’s active c5 break and reducing tactical threats that led to your resignation.

lichess_summary.session_summary: AKK_010’s lone loss came from a sloppy opening choice—he entered a dubious King’s Gambit line and never recovered, exposing his king and surrendering central control within ten moves. The pattern shows he cannot handle unorthodox, aggressive openings; he must abandon speculative gambits and stick to solid, theory‑backed systems like the Caro‑Kann or the London System to build a reliable pawn structure. Immediate action: study the first 15 moves of the Caro‑Kann Defense, memorize the key defensive motifs, and practice them in at least five rapid games before attempting any risky opening again.
